Docs.Title: Documentation
Docs.Intro: Rendering, color precision, dithering and playback workarounds.
Docs.Pipeline.Title: How the LUT reaches the screen
Docs.Pipeline.Body: A buffer is an image stored in GPU memory. An app draws a frame into its buffer. Windows usually combines that frame with other windows in DWM, the desktop compositor. DWM LUT changes the colors in the composed image before it is presented. A 3D LUT maps each input RGB color to a calibrated output color. It does not change the monitor's hardware settings.
Docs.DirectX.Title: DirectX 11 and DirectX 12
Docs.DirectX.Body: DirectX is the API an app uses to draw. Our shader runs later, in DWM, so composed DirectX 12 content can receive the same correction as DirectX 11 content. The native hook still uses D3D11 resources. DirectX 12 does not automatically fix a buffer or choose a better bit depth. Fullscreen and borderless frames can use DirectFlip, Independent Flip or hardware overlays to reach the screen without our composed buffer. That bypass is the limitation, regardless of the drawing API. PresentMon can identify the actual presentation path.
Docs.Precision.Title: 8-bit and 10-bit SDR
Docs.Precision.Body: 8 bits store 256 values per RGB channel. 10 bits store 1024, so adjacent shades can be closer together. This is a count of stored values, not a measured score of monitor quality. We read the DWM texture's DXGI format: an 8-bit UNORM buffer uses 255 rounding intervals; R10G10B10A2 uses 1023. Windows and the driver choose that buffer format. DWM LUT does not switch your display link to 10 bits. A 10-bit monitor may still receive an image that passed through an 8-bit buffer. The old SDR shader forced an 8-bit grid even on a 10-bit target; the current shader preserves that target's available precision.
Docs.Hdr.Title: HDR and floating-point buffers
Docs.Hdr.Body: HDR needs a LUT calibrated for HDR. The native path converts the scRGB image into the HDR LUT's PQ/BT.2100 domain, applies the LUT, then returns floating-point scRGB to DWM. FP16 means 16 floating-point bits per channel; it does not mean the monitor has 16-bit output. Windows and the driver later convert to the display's signal format. The SDR 8/10-bit rounding and error-diffusion modes are not applied to HDR. Final display conversion can still involve quantization and dithering, but this hook does not control or measure that final stage. No extra HDR error diffusion has been implemented.
Docs.Dithering.Title: Blue noise and error diffusion
Docs.Dithering.Body: Dithering distributes rounding error so a gradient is less likely to show visible steps. It cannot recover detail already lost in the source. Blue noise uses a fixed pattern and processes pixels independently; it is the default with low GPU cost. Error diffusion passes a pixel's rounding error to later pixels. Our optional Sierra Lite version works inside 32 × 32 blocks. Errors reset at block and updated-region edges, so the pattern can show boundaries or shimmer during motion. It uses more GPU time and memory and is not guaranteed to look better. Unsupported compute resources fall back to blue noise.
Docs.FourK.Title: 4K and refresh rate
Docs.FourK.Body: 3840 × 2160 contains about 8.3 million pixels, four times as many as 1920 × 1080. The tiled algorithm can process 4K landscape and portrait buffers without storing a whole image's errors in shared memory. Its extra FP16 image is about 63 MiB at 4K. Frame budgets shrink as refresh rate rises: 16.67 ms at 60 Hz, 8.33 ms at 120 Hz and 4.17 ms at 240 Hz, shared with all other GPU work. Fitting in memory does not prove smooth playback. Performance on the affected laptop has not been measured. Use blue noise if error diffusion causes stutter.
Docs.Playback.Title: MPC-HC, MPC Video Renderer and madVR
Docs.Playback.Body: The reporter confirmed that MPC Video Renderer with Swap effect set to Discard keeps the SDR LUT active in fullscreen. Flip still loses it when the seekbar hides. Discard is an optional SDR workaround; MPCVR forces Flip for HDR output. The madVR fullscreen issue remains. A safe general workaround is to disable DWM LUT during the viewing session and enable madVR's own calibration LUT for that whole session, then re-enable DWM LUT afterwards. Use a madVR-compatible LUT export; renaming a .cube file is not a conversion. The reporter also uses a fullscreen profile, but a fullscreen rule alone cannot detect the seekbar's composition changes. Avoid applying the same calibration twice. An exclusive-mode label does not prove true exclusive scanout. These are workarounds, not a confirmed universal fullscreen fix.
Docs.Shortcuts.Title: Keyboard shortcuts and saved state
Docs.Shortcuts.Body: Not assigned is a status, not a button. Edit records a shortcut; Save registers it with Windows. Remove unregisters it and deletes the saved assignment. The two actions need different combinations. If Windows or another app owns a combination, registration fails and the previous assignments are restored when possible. The cycle action chooses the next saved SDR LUT for the selected display. It does not cycle HDR LUTs. Correction settings and shortcuts are stored in state.json under %AppData%\DwmLutModern; disabling correction keeps it disabled after restart.
